finding: src/anomaly/state.py:15 Attempt failures persist common credentials because the central error sanitizer recognizes only three token prefixes.
rationale: The public workflow can pass an arbitrary dynamic-owner exception directly into durable attempt recording, and the only sanitizer on that path recognizes three provider prefixes, so common credentials remain reachable and are persisted repeatedly without an upstream guard or fail-safe.

evidence.output: safe_error calls _safe_text, which applies redact_credentials and _SECRET; both credential regexes match only sk_live_, ghp_, and github_pat_, with no assignment, Bearer, AWS, Slack, or credential-bearing URL handling.

run_workflow is the public entry point, invokes the caller-supplied reasoning callback without constraining exception text, and run_attempts catches any Exception; _record_failure then writes the sanitized message to failure.json, events.jsonl, state.failures, and blocked_reason after the third attempt.

review.py already redacts sensitive assignments, Bearer values, Slack xox tokens, and AWS AKIA keys, while the installed workflow contract requires credential-redacted failure persistence and forbids credentials in case JSON or events; no equivalent protection exists on the attempt-error path.
